richText: A bean is an object managed by Spring.
The application context creates beans, supplies their dependencies, and manages their lifecycle.
Component scanning searches selected packages for classes marked with component annotations. It registers bean definitions for those classes.
By default, a bean has singleton scope: one instance per bean definition in an application context. Singleton scope does not make mutable fields thread-safe.
@Component marks a general component. @Service marks a class containing application operations.
@Repository marks a data-access component. It supports persistence-exception translation when that infrastructure is configured.
@Service does not automatically start a transaction. These annotations do not require particular folder names.
The application class’s package and its subpackages are scanned by default. Classes elsewhere need explicit registration or a wider scan.

example.title: Register a greeting service
description: Place this class in the application package or a subpackage.
explanation: Spring discovers GreetingService during component scanning.
Spring creates a GreetingService bean. Registering it does not call greet().

richText: Register an object from a method
@Configuration marks a class containing bean definitions.
@Bean registers the object returned by a method. Use it when you need to construct an object explicitly, including a class from a library.

example.title: Register a Clock bean
description: A Clock supplies the current time. This configuration registers a UTC Clock for injection.
explanation: Spring calls the bean method to obtain the Clock instance.
Another bean can request Clock as a constructor parameter.
